sections.title: Divisions in the Church
observations: Paul addresses the issue of divisions among the Corinthians, emphasizing that they are acting like mere humans rather than spiritual beings.
He points out that their allegiance to different leaders (Paul, Apollos, Cephas) is a sign of immaturity in their faith.
The church is not built on human leaders but on Christ, who is the foundation of their faith.

sections.title: The Role of Leaders
observations: Paul explains that he and Apollos are merely servants through whom the Corinthians came to believe.
He uses the metaphor of planting and watering to illustrate their roles in the growth of the church, but emphasizes that it is God who gives the growth.
This teaches the importance of humility among church leaders and the recognition that all success comes from God.

sections.title: The Church as God's Temple
observations: Paul shifts the metaphor to that of a temple, stating that the church is God's temple and that the Spirit of God dwells within it.
He warns against destroying God's temple, which can refer to both the individual believer and the corporate church.
This section highlights the sanctity of the church and the seriousness of how believers treat one another.

importantVerses.commentary: For you are still of the flesh. For while there is jealousy and strife among you, are you not of the flesh and behaving only in a human way?
So neither he who plants nor he who waters is anything, but only God who gives the growth.
Do you not know that you are God's temple and that God's Spirit dwells in you?

questions: What does it mean to be spiritually mature versus immature in the context of the church?
How can we apply the principle of humility in leadership within our own church communities?
In what ways can we ensure that we are building on the foundation of Christ in our lives and ministries?
